title: Engine Identity, Lubrication and Valve Timing
introduction:
I use this overview to connect the engine’s identity with what happens inside it. Start with the identification labels, use the cylinder illustration as a layout map, then follow the lubrication drawing to see which components depend on the oil supply. Oil has quite the job description here: it lubricates moving parts, supplies cooling jets and helps operate the cam-timing system.

Match each drawing’s callouts to its accompanying table; the label key and lubrication key belong to different illustrations. Read the cylinder layout in the orientation shown. This overview explains identification and operation; it does not provide a firing order, oil-pressure test, service specifications or a repair sequence.

edits.text: Meet the Engine
edits.why: Start with the engine’s construction and equipment before exploring its lubrication and valve timing.

edits.text: The 3.7L (4V) is a V-6 engine with the following construction, fuel, ignition and timing features:
edits.why: These features identify the engine arrangement covered by this overview.

edits.text: Dual overhead camshafts control the valves.
edits.why: The camshaft lobes sit directly above mechanical buckets on top of the valves. That is the supported physical relationship to keep in mind.

edits.text: Four valves serve each cylinder.
edits.why: Intake valves admit the fresh charge, while exhaust valves let burned gases leave.

edits.text: Sequential Multi-Port Fuel Injection (SFI) supplies the fuel.
edits.why: This identifies the fuel-injection system fitted to the engine; the overview does not describe injector testing.

edits.text: The intake manifold has composite upper and lower sections.
edits.why: The manifold distributes incoming air to the cylinders.

edits.text: The cylinder head is aluminum.
edits.why: The head contains the valves and forms the top of the combustion chambers. It is a separate casting from the cylinder block.

edits.text: An aluminum, 60-degree V-cylinder block forms the engine’s main structure.
edits.why: The block contains the cylinders and supports the crankshaft, which receives piston force through the connecting rods.

edits.text: The accessory drive belt drives the coolant pump.
edits.why: Keep this external belt drive distinct from the internal timing chains that synchronize crankshaft and camshaft movement.

edits.text: Twin independent variable cam timing (Ti-VCT) adjusts valve timing.
edits.why: Intake and exhaust camshaft timing can be controlled separately, allowing valve events to change with operating needs.

edits.text: Electronic ignition uses 6 coil-on-plug ignition coils.
edits.why: The name describes the arrangement: the ignition coils are positioned at the spark plugs.

edits.text: Identify the Engine
I start quick engine identification with the safety certification decal.
edits.why: Establishing engine identity helps keep a familiar-looking engine cover from becoming the basis for choosing service information.

edits.text: Find the decal on the LH front door lock face panel.
edits.why: This vehicle decal is separate from the engine code information label described next.

edits.text: Read the Engine Code Information Label
Find the engine code information label on the front side of the valve cover. Match the illustrated label’s callouts to the accompanying table to understand its fields.
edits.why: I use the illustration to learn the layout, then read the label on the engine for its actual identifying information. The printed example is not the identity of every engine.

edits.text: Read the Cylinder Identification Drawing
edits.why: Match each marked cylinder to its position in the illustrated bank, keeping the drawing in the orientation shown. The image does not mark the vehicle-front direction, so it should not be used to invent that orientation or a firing order.

edits.text: How the Engine Systems Work
Trace the Lubrication System
edits.why: I begin at the oil pan at the bottom of the drawing and follow the arrowheads through the pickup and pump, then trace the filter circuit and branches through the block and cylinder heads. Use the accompanying table to identify each callout. The separated components make the connections visible; their spacing is not an installation guide.

edits.text: How the Oil Pump Supplies the Engine

This is a force-feed lubrication system: oil is supplied under full pressure to the crankshaft, connecting rod bearings, timing chain tensioners, piston oil cooling jets and VCT solenoids. A restricting orifice in the cylinder head’s front camshaft cap controls oil flow to the valve tappets and valve train.
edits.why: Think of the oil passages as a distribution network with metered branches. The oil supply serves loaded bearings, cooling jets and timing components, so its job reaches well beyond making surfaces slippery.

edits.text: The lubrication system is designed to deliver the oil flow critical engine components need throughout the engine’s operating range.
edits.why: That operating range matters: the system has to supply its consumers as engine speed and operating conditions change.

edits.text: A positive displacement internal gear oil pump provides the system’s oil flow.
edits.why: Oil flow supplies the lubrication passages. Oil pressure describes that supply under operating conditions; the amount of oil sitting in the pan is a different piece of information.

edits.text: This internal-gear design is called a gerotor pump. Its mounting, drive and pressure-control arrangements work as follows:
edits.why: The following details connect the pump’s location and mechanical drive with its ability to supply oil across the operating range.

edits.text: The oil pump mounts on the front face of the cylinder block.
edits.why: Use this location to recognize the pump in the lubrication drawing.

edits.text: The inner rotor is centered on the crankshaft post and driven by flats on the crankshaft.
edits.why: This mechanical connection makes the crankshaft drive the pump’s inner rotor.

edits.text: An integral, internally vented relief valve limits system pressure by routing bypassed oil back to the pump’s inlet side.
edits.why: The return path explains how the pump controls pressure while continuing to circulate oil.

edits.text: The pump’s displacement is selected to provide enough oil volume for correct pressure at both hot idle and maximum speed.
edits.why: Displacement concerns the volume the pump moves. Adequate delivery has to cover the engine’s operating range, including these different speed conditions.

edits.text: The relief valve’s calibration protects the lubrication system from excessive pressure when oil viscosity is high.
edits.why: Higher-viscosity oil resists flow more strongly, making pressure control an essential part of the supply system.

edits.text: The relief valve is also designed to maintain adequate connecting rod bearing lubrication under high-temperature and high-speed conditions.
edits.why: Pressure control must still leave the bearings adequately supplied when the engine is hot and turning quickly.

edits.text: How the Valve Train Acts on the Valves
The valve train uses direct acting mechanical buckets (DAMB). Each camshaft lobe sits directly above a mechanical bucket, and the bucket sits on top of its valve.
edits.why: Picture the bucket as the contact piece between the shaped cam lobe and the valve. This arrangement explains how camshaft motion acts on the valves; it does not provide a valve-clearance adjustment procedure.

edits.text: How Twin Independent Variable Cam Timing (Ti-VCT) Helps

Twin independent VCT controls intake and exhaust camshaft timing separately, allowing valve-closing timing and valve overlap to vary. This optimizes combustion at full load for improved power and low-speed torque across a broader torque curve. Variable overlap also improves fuel economy and emissions, while optimized cold-start operation improves exhaust emissions.
edits.why: I think of this as changing the valves’ appointment times to suit the engine’s workload. The mechanical buckets transmit cam-lobe movement; variable cam timing changes when those valve events happen.
